prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Business Rules Registry: thresholds, connection/gate/towing/stand/swap rules, border states, CTT tolerance, per-state tie-breaker permission. Modes: Normal; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction(binding metering; RFM may suspend swaps); Recovery; Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms); Contingency Fallback(ADM declares after RFM, Tower Supervisor, SSE). Fallback: Foxglove down→Digital Briefing Room; Marlinstone/CAM unreliable→last verified Airport Capacity Plan; Blueharbor down→Slot Coordinator manual sheet at Contingency Operations Console, keeps last valid CTT; revised CTT needs Tower Supervisor+Ramp Control Lead, AOC readback; Ironleaf advisory; Emberline monitor-only; reconcile with Slot Allocation Engine; conflicts→Collaborative Decision Log; Performance Analytics Warehouse→Post Operations Report. Connection risk advisory: AOC sends Passenger Misconnect Count→Airline Interface Adapter validates; Marlinstone computes sensitivity; tie-breaker only if Registry permits; Departure Metering Service recommends; Tower Supervisor may reject. Security: Identity Access Service(IAS) authoritative for accounts/roles/sessions; individual identity, no shared accounts, least privilege; rapid suspension; temporary access needs sponsor, purpose, scope, expiry, review. Roles: RFM authorizes regional measures; Slot Coordinator administers slots within Registry; Tower Supervisor operates Tower Sequence Manager, cannot change airline priorities/entitlements; Ramp Control Lead updates Ramp Movement Board only; AOC, Aircraft Operator Rep view/submit, no admin; SSE technical admin separate from operational approval; Data Governance Steward manages retention/reference data/audit review, no traffic instructions. No single user creates+approves+conceals GDP, AAR or Tactical Regulation Proposal changes; Regional Flow Platform records initiator, approver, object, effective time. Warehouse: analytical roles only, cannot alter Audit Event Ledger. Ledger logs authentication, role/privilege changes, approvals, config, exports, emergency access; Time Synchronization Service timestamps; protected; retention agreed by airport operator, regional authority, aircraft operators. Monitoring alerts SSE and Steward. Silverpine accepts emergency access only after IAS records incident reference+expiry. Aliases: RFM=Regional Flow Manager; ADM=Airport Duty Manager; AOC=Airline Operations Coordinator; SSE=System Support Engineer.

Document units:
S784: Emergency access may be granted to the Emergency Response Coordinator, Airport Duty Manager, or System Support Engineer when life safety, airport continuity, or critical system recovery requires immediate action.
S785: Use of emergency access shall generate prominent audit events and shall require post-event review by the Data Governance Steward and the responsible operational authority.
S786: During Contingency Fallback State, access control shall continue to enforce role separation even when some integrations are unavailable and manual coordination becomes necessary.
S787: When normal connectivity is restored, the Regional Flow Platform shall reconcile contingency actions with the Collaborative Decision Log so that accountability is preserved across the full incident timeline.
S788: After connectivity is restored, audit processing shall treat reconciled contingency actions as part of the same operational record as actions taken during Normal Operations.
S789: The Regional Flow Platform shall record slot compliance events in the Audit Event Ledger using the operating date, flight identifier, airport, runway direction, and applicable regulation reference.
S790: Each compliance assessment shall compare the Calculated Takeoff Time, the Target Off Block Time, actual off-block time, and actual takeoff time against the tolerance defined in the Business Rules Registry.
S791: The Slot Compliance State shall indicate whether a flight was compliant, early, late, exempted, substituted, cancelled, or pending review at the end of the traffic period.
S792: The Audit Event Ledger shall preserve the time source applied by the Time Synchronization Service so that later review can distinguish operational delay from data latency.
S793: User decisions entered through the Airport CDM Portal shall be linked to the authenticated role provided by the Identity Access Service.
S794: The Collaborative Decision Log shall retain the stated reason, decision time, affected flight, and visible operational context for each material change to a slot or sequence.
S795: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the permission email to justify an approved slot substitution during post-operations review.
S796: Substitution records shall show the original flight, replacement flight, assigned Calculated Takeoff Time, acceptance status, and any subsequent cancellation or reversion.
S797: When an Aircraft Operator Representative proposes a substitution, the audit trail shall capture whether the change preserved the constraints of the active Ground Delay Program.
S798: The Slot Coordinator shall review substitution activity after operations to confirm that priority rules were applied consistently across participating operators.
S799: Late operational changes shall be distinguished from planned updates by comparing the change timestamp with the freeze horizon held in the Business Rules Registry.
